info.title: Hunter-Seeker Agent Actions (curated)
info.description: Deterministic, signed, refusable decisions for agents. Agents may generate copy; they may not invent the score. Deprecation policy: a contract version is served for 12 months after its successor ships.

post.summary: Discover the pattern and rank a table (one billed run). Add refit_of to refresh an analysis.
post.description: Existing tool; schemas are exported from the product's MCP server (packages/mcp/scripts/export-tool-schemas.mts).

post.summary: Score one entity at decision time
post.description: Costs ONE DECISION from your quota (never a run). Score ONE row against a scorecard the engine already fitted — use the model_ref that a cleared hs_rank_topk returned. Returns the calibrated score (0–1), an engine-authored band (act = certified likely; escalate = uncertain, ask a human; refuse = the engine will not vouch, with a reason), a max_autonomy hint (L0–L4: how much rope THIS decision earns), up to four principal_reasons (engine-ordered levers in the shape adverse-action rules require), and a SIGNED Verdict you can hand to a reviewer or verify with hs_verify_verdict. The score is byte-identical to what the originating run would have assigned this row: the scorecard is a cache of a deterministic fit, not a second model. Best for: 'should my agent act on this lead / account / ticket right now'. Not for: rows from a different table than the model_ref was fitted on (columns must match). Firewall: no thresholds, weights, or condition counts are returned — read band and principal_reasons, never try to reconstruct the rule. subject_kind 'person' REQUIRES acknowledge_decision_support: true and caps max_autonomy at L2 (L0 without a human principal). A refuse band bills nothing. Common mistakes: reusing an expired model_ref (404 model_ref_expired → re-run hs_rank_topk, do not retry); treating band as advice — it is a fact about likelihood; on an adverse outcome 'act' means likely to churn/default/fail, on a desirable one likely to convert/renew — read verdict.outcome.polarity.

x-mcp-annotations.title: Score one entity at decision time

row.description: One entity's feature values, same columns as the fitted table.

post.description: Free; no API key needed; no engine run. Check that a Verdict was issued by Hunter-Seeker and has not been altered. Pass the verdict object and its signature exactly as received. Returns status: valid | invalid_signature | expired | unknown_key — and nothing else, so the endpoint cannot be probed. Best for: an approval step that must prove the score was not authored by the agent; an auditor; another vendor's agent. The same check runs offline with the open-source libraries hs-verify (pip) and @hunter-seeker/verify (npm) against the public keys at hunter-seeker.net/.well-known/jwks.json. Common mistakes: re-serialising the verdict before verifying (pass the object, the verifier canonicalises it — RFC 8785); treating 'expired' as valid — an expired verdict is re-scored, never reused.

Free; writes YOUR observed outcomes (never fires an action, never retrains). For entities scored under a model_ref, append what actually happened: outcome is a binary (0/1, true/false, yes/no); observed_at is when you observed it; event_id is your idempotency key (send the same id on retry and the row is written once). Outcomes are EVIDENCE for hs_action_evidence and drift signals for hs_drift_status; they never change the scorecard, the band, or the pattern — a refit is an explicit hs_rank_topk with refit_of. Free text is refused (422 outcome_malformed) so this ledger cannot become a transcript store. Best for: closing the loop after acting, so the engine can tell you whether acting worked. Common mistakes: inferring the outcome from the trace or the agent's own judgement — report the real-world binary you observed; sending prose.

bearer.description: Machine key hsk_live_… or hsk_test_… ; scopes read, run, write:outcomes, admin:keys

provenance.description: The engine build that produced these facts. Present on every response.

fetch_url.description: Public https URL to retrieve the dataset from. Omit to receive an upload_url instead.

direct_upload.description: Direct-to-storage upload is now the DEFAULT (no size or row cap), so you rarely need this. Set false to instead receive a proxied upload_url, which normalizes a JSON body to CSV but is capped at the ~4.5MB serverless body limit. Ignored when fetch_url is present.

dataset_id.description: Pass this as data.dataset_id to hs_rank_topk.

upload_url.description: PUT the raw CSV/JSON bytes here before ranking.

provenance.description: The engine build that produced these facts. Present on every response.

rows.description: Inline JSON rows (SYNCHRONOUS — the ranking returns immediately). Best for a few hundred rows: the data rides inside your tool-call payload, so your CLIENT's per-message budget (Claude Code ~25k tokens, Claude Desktop ~150k chars) usually binds well before the server ceiling (~4MB / 2000 rows / 64 columns). Each row is one entity observation. For anything medium or larger, use dataset_id / fetch_url / direct_upload.

csv.description: Inline CSV text — header row + data rows (SYNCHRONOUS). Same small-inline budget as rows; a convenience when you already hold CSV. For anything larger, use dataset_id / fetch_url / direct_upload.

fetch_url.description: Public https URL the SERVER fetches, parses, and ranks in ONE async call (collapses hs_provide_dataset + hs_rank_topk). Returns { status:"pending", task_id } — poll hs_poll_task. Internal/private/non-https URLs are refused.

dataset_id.description: A dataset already registered via hs_provide_dataset (upload or fetch), for larger data. ASYNC — returns { status:"pending", task_id }; poll hs_poll_task.

direct_upload.description: Set true to receive a direct-to-storage PUT URL (upload_url + dataset_id) for a large dataset (~1M rows), bypassing the inline/proxy caps. NO ranking starts: PUT your CSV, then call hs_rank_topk again with the returned dataset_id.

data.description: Exactly one data source: rows or csv (small, inline, synchronous) | fetch_url or dataset_id (async, poll hs_poll_task) | direct_upload:true (get an upload URL — no run starts).

outcome_column.description: The column holding the yes/no result to learn to predict. Must be known historically - not derived after the outcome (that is leakage).

entity_column.description: What each row represents, e.g. customer_id, machine_id, application_id.

subject_kind.description: What kind of thing each entity is. "person" enables decision-support safeguards.

horizon.description: The time window the prediction is about, e.g. "30 days".

k.description: How many top entities to return (default 20, max 100).

acknowledge_decision_support.description: Required true when subject_kind is "person" and the outcome is in a regulated domain (hiring, credit, education, insurance, benefits, justice). Confirms results are decision-support with human review.

idempotency_key.description: For dataset_id runs: reuse to dedupe retried submissions onto the same task.

kind.description: A kind id from hs_describe_capabilities → readings.kinds (e.g. "sequential").

version.description: The kind version, from the same list.

roles.description: This kind’s role names mapped to YOUR column names, e.g. {"identifier":"customer_id","time_axis":"ts","event_type":"event"}. Nothing is inferred — every required_role must appear.

params.description: Validated ENGINE-side against the kind’s param_schema. A bad value returns a named 422 and the run is refunded.

label.description: The outcome predicate, as data, e.g. {"kind":"lapsed"}. Your meaning, never ours.

as_of.description: ISO-8601 cutoff. Omit and the engine computes it from your data and RETURNS it.

reading.description: Reduce an EVENT table to one row per entity BEFORE ranking. Omit when your rows are already one per entity.

ranking_ref.description: Reuse this for the free drill-in tools for one hour.

model_ref.description: The fitted scorecard behind this ranking. Pass it to hs_score_entity to decide about a single entity. NULL means the engine minted none for this run — re-run rather than guessing a ref.

entities.description: The ranked page, highest likelihood first.

validation.description: How the model was validated. scheme "none" means no rows could be held back, and n_holdout is then null (not 0) with a reason.

gate_verdicts.description: The engine-recorded gate decisions behind this answer.

leak_guard.description: Columns quarantined as likely target leakage, each with a plain-English reason. NULL means there was no finding (honest-null) — never that leakage was checked and found clean.

entity_replication.description: The SHAPE of the data behind this ranking. n_rows far above n_entities means the same entity sat on many rows — which leak_guard cannot tell you, because it catches a leaky COLUMN, not a leaky SPLIT.

next.description: What you can do with this ranking, and which of those cost nothing.

leak_warnings.description: Local heuristic pre-flags of obviously post-outcome column names. Not a guarantee, and not a substitute for leak_guard.

disclaimer.description: Present on an acknowledged regulated-domain run. Surface it to the user.

result.description: Present and "none" when the data did not clear the lift bar. This is a real answer, not a failure: relay the reasons, do not retry.

status.description: The run has not finished. Poll hs_poll_task after retry_after_ms; do not tight-loop.

deduped.description: An identical submit was already in flight; this is that same task, not a second run.

status_url.description: Short-TTL signed link to a live status page a human can open.

stage.description: Leak-firewalled progress — never a partial ranking.

category_match.description: Read literally and never drop the negation: "is_not_one_of" names the opposite cohort from "is_one_of".

pattern.description: ONE joint pattern. Read the conditions as a single combination; never rank them or report one alone.

association_not_causal.description: Always true. Levers are what the model associates with a different outcome, never proven interventions.

likelihood_direction.description: Which way this change moves PREDICTED LIKELIHOOD. A fact, not a recommendation, and NOT fixed to "lower" — read it per lever.

reason.description: Present only when levers is empty, saying which honest-empty case this is.
